results.title: One GPU, five “current” prices: how to tell which rental price is real | GPUJournal
highlights:
Search for an H100 rental price and you will meet several different numbers, every one of them presented as current. In late October 2026 we counted five different on-demand prices for the same H100 on a single provider’s own pages — on the same day. This guide puts the stated figures next to the verified ones, names the five mechanisms that pile prices up around one GPU, and ends with the three-step check that separates a price from a claim.

### The verdict

- H100 SXM — Stated on Spheron’s own pages: $2.64, $2.65, $2.75 and $2.98/hr on-demand across pages stamped Oct 20–28, 2026 — and $4.20/hr on pages refreshed Oct 28; spot stated $2.21/hr (Oct 28), then $2.79/hr (Oct 29). Verified best offer: TensorDock $2.25/GPU/hr at an 8-GPU minimum — an $18.00/hr floor; cheapest single card, RunPod Community $2.69/hr. Five stated on-demand figures live at once on Oct 28 — a $1.56 spread; the highest stated figure sits 56% above the cheapest verified single-card price. · $2.25/hr at TensorDock
- B200 — Stated on Spheron’s own pages: $9.80–$9.90/hr on-demand (Oct 20), $11.06 (Oct 21), $11.12 (Oct 22, still stated Oct 30) — and on Oct 31 its own pages disagreed again: $11.06 on most pages, $11.12 in its refresh post; spot stated at $5.31 and $6.12 on the same day (Oct 24). Verified best offer: RunPod Community $5.98/hr. The stated on-demand price runs $5.14/hr above the verified best offer — 86% more for the same card. · $5.98/hr at RunPod Community
- H200 — Stated on Spheron’s own pages: $7.09 and $5.54/hr on the same day (Oct 27); $4.80 and $5.51/hr inside a single refresh post (Oct 31). Verified best offer: RunPod Community $3.59/hr. Same-day stated figures $1.55 apart; the highest stated figure is nearly double the verified best offer. · $3.59/hr at RunPod Community
- RTX 4090 — No split in our record. The two prices you will meet most are both verified, and both sit on RunPod’s own pricing page — Community $0.34/hr (Best offer) and Secure $0.89/hr are different service tiers, not a disagreement. No gap to explain: two real prices, each labelled with what it buys. Multiplicity only becomes a problem when the labels and the dates go missing. · $0.34/hr at RunPod Community

## Prices for the cards in this guide

The board's current prices — checked nov 14, 2026.

TensorDock H100 SXM · 80GB 8-GPU minimum Best offer$18.00 / hr total

On-demand 8-GPU minimum — $2.25 / GPU / hr equivalent Checked Nov 14, 2026 Launch ↗

RunPod Community B200 · 192GB Best offer$5.98 / GPU / hr On-demand Checked Nov 14, 2026 Launch ↗

RunPod Community H200 · 141GB Best offer$3.59 / GPU / hr On-demand Checked Nov 14, 2026 Launch ↗

On-demand Checked Nov 14, 2026 Launch ↗

## Why one GPU has five prices

Two words on this page carry exact meanings. Stated means a figure a site publishes, reported here exactly as stated, with its source and date — never as a verified price. Verified means read by us on the provider’s own current pricing page and re-checked on Oct 31, 2026. Five mechanisms produce the pile-up. None of them requires anyone to invent a number — pages are written at different times, updated on different schedules, and quoted figures age at different speeds. Each mechanism below is illustrated with figures we read first-hand, on the dates printed.

### 1 · Pages refreshed at different times — the H100 on Spheron’s own pages

A site with hundreds of pages does not update them all at once, so yesterday’s price survives on the pages nobody has touched yet. The H100 on Spheron’s own pages, read across eleven days:

| Date read | Stated on-demand (Spheron’s pages) | Stated spot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 20, 2026 | $2.64, $2.65, $2.75 and $2.98/hr — four figures, different pages, the same day’s stamp | — |
| Through Oct 27 | $2.64/hr | $1.84/hr |
| Oct 28, 2026 | $4.20/hr on refreshed pages (its specs, slow-inference and multi-node guides and its pricing FAQ) — while the four older figures were still live on other pages: five stated on-demand prices at once | $2.21/hr |
| Oct 29, 2026 | $4.20/hr on the refreshed pages, $2.64/hr still standing elsewhere | $2.79/hr |

No single row of that table can honestly be quoted as “the” Spheron H100 price — and that is the point. A renter landing on any one page meets exactly one figure, presented as current, with no way to tell whether it is the newest or the oldest on the site.

...

### 3 · A per-GPU price can hide a per-node minimum

TensorDock’s H100 rate — $2.25 per GPU per hour — is the lowest verified per-GPU H100 price in our checks, and it is quoted at an eight-GPU minimum, which makes the real entry ticket $18.00 an hour:

| Route | Per-GPU price | What you must take | Real hourly floor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TensorDock — H100 SXM | $2.25/GPU/hr | 8 GPUs minimum | $18.00/hr |
| RunPod Community — H100 SXM | $2.69/hr | A single card | $2.69/hr |

The figure is real; the shape is the story. We priced that shape in full in our TensorDock pricing guide, so this page only borrows its headline: a per-GPU number means nothing until you know how many GPUs you must take with it.

...

### How we know

Every stated Spheron figure in this guide was read on Spheron’s own pages (spheron.network) between Oct 20 and Oct 31, 2026, and is carried in our Price Watch with its read date: the H100 on-demand set ($2.64, $2.65, $2.75, $2.98, all stamped Oct 20, 2026; $4.20 on pages refreshed Oct 28); H100 spot ($1.84 through Oct 27; $2.21 read Oct 28; $2.79 read Oct 29); B200 on-demand ($9.80–$9.90 stated Oct 20; $11.06 stated Oct 21; $11.12 stated Oct 22 and still stated Oct 30; $11.06 on most pages vs $11.12 in its refresh post, read Oct 31); B200 spot ($5.31 and $6.12, both stated Oct 24); H200 ($7.09 and $5.54, both stated Oct 27; $4.80 and $5.51 in one refresh post, read Oct 31); RTX 6000 Ada spot $0.93 above on-demand $0.78 on one page stamped Oct 22; and the pricing FAQ’s rival quotes, dated May 2026 on Spheron’s pages. Together AI’s tiers were read on together.ai/pricing on Oct 31, 2026, and its “starting at $6.79” advertisement was seen the same day. The verified column is our board check of Oct 31, 2026: TensorDock H100 SXM $2.25/GPU/hr at an 8-GPU minimum (terms read on TensorDock’s own H100 page, Oct 29, 2026); RunPod Community H100 SXM $2.69, B200 $5.98, H200 $3.59, RTX 4090 $0.34; RunPod Secure RTX 4090 $0.89, B200 $7.99; Lambda B200 $6.69; Nebius B200 $8.50. The gap arithmetic: $4.20 vs $2.69 is 56% above; $11.12 vs $5.98 is $5.14/hr, or 86%, above; $7.09 is 1.97× $3.59 (“nearly double”); $7.09 − $5.54 = $1.55; the FAQ gaps are $7.99 − $5.89 = $2.10, $6.69 − $5.29/$4.99 = $1.40–$1.70, and $8.50 − $5.50 = $3.00. Two things this guide deliberately does not claim: that any stated figure is what a checkout on Spheron’s own platform would charge — we cannot verify that, and the inability is the finding — and that any provider intends to mislead. Pages age at different speeds; the dated record is what we publish.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

Published rate cards tell a different story from marketplaces. Our price board — built from the on-demand prices cloud providers publish — put the on-demand H100 hour at $4.11 on 13 Nov 2026, against a marketplace median of $3.93 in the week of 9 Nov 2026.

Neither number is “the” price. List prices show what providers ask for capacity on demand; marketplace medians show where spare capacity clears; reserved and contract prices, usually lower again, sit in agreements that are rarely published in full. For anyone valuing a neocloud, lending against GPUs or underwriting a datacentre lease, the spread between the three says how tight capacity is.

results.title: GPU rental prices are rising in 2026 — the dated evidence | GPUJournal
highlights:
### The verdict

- Nebius — Raised rates across the board. H100 SXM now $4.50/hr.
- RunPod Secure — Raised Secure Cloud rates. H200 $4.59 → $5.29/hr (▲ 15%); RTX 4090 $0.74 → $0.89/hr (▲ 20%).
- Verda — Three rises in four days — all nine rose on Oct 23 and Oct 26; seven of nine rose again on Oct 24. H100 SXM $4.34 → $4.61/hr (▲ 6.2%).
- The cheapest offers — No movement in our records. The best verified H100 offer is still $2.25/hr.

## The evidence, date by date

Every rise below was read on the provider's own published pricing page on both sides of the change — the before figure and the after figure, each with its date. That is the standard our Price Watch applies to every entry. October 1 — Nebius raises across the board: Nebius lifted its on-demand rates at the start of October, and our board carries the post-rise rates (H100 $4.50/hr, H200 $5.40/hr, B200 $8.50/hr, verified Oct 19 and re-read unchanged Oct 26). October 14 — RunPod Secure goes up: RTX 4090 rose from $0.74 to $0.89/hr (▲ 20%) and H200 from $4.59 to $5.29/hr (▲ 15%) on RunPod's Secure Cloud; both rates were re-read on RunPod's own page on Oct 24 and Oct 26 — unchanged since the rise. October 23, 24 and 26 — Verda rises three times in four days: all nine Verda GPUs rose on Oct 23 and again on Oct 26, and seven of the nine rose on Oct 24 as well (A100 40GB and L40S held that day) — the full table is below. We are not the only ones seeing it: a third-party analysis published Oct 21, 2026 found H100 prices up at six of seven specialist GPU clouds during 2026. Our own records cover October in daily detail; the direction agrees.

### Verda — three rises in four days, in full

All figures USD per GPU per hour, read on verda.com/pricing on each date shown.

| GPU | Oct 22 | Oct 23 | Oct 24 | Oct 26 | 4-day move |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $4.34 | $4.51 | $4.56 | $4.61 | ▲ 6.2% |
| H200 | $5.66 | $5.89 | $5.95 | $6.01 | ▲ 6.2% |
| B200 | $8.07 | $8.36 | $8.44 | $8.52 | ▲ 5.6% |
| B300 | $10.28 | $10.69 | $10.80 | $10.91 | ▲ 6.1% |
| GB300 | $11.82 | $12.29 | $12.42 | $12.55 | ▲ 6.2% |
| A100 80GB | $2.07 | $2.13 | $2.15 | $2.16 | ▲ 4.3% |
| A100 40GB | $1.52 | $1.56 | $1.56 | $1.58 | ▲ 3.9% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | $2.40 | $2.49 | $2.52 | $2.54 | ▲ 5.8% |
| L40S | $1.77 | $1.81 | $1.81 | $1.83 | ▲ 3.4% |

### The half that has not moved

Against those rises, the cheapest verified offers on our board did not move at all during the week of Oct 19–26:

| GPU | Best verified offer | Provider | Oct 19 → Oct 26 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $2.25/hr | TensorDock (8-GPU minimum) | — unchanged |
| H200 | $3.59/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| B200 | $5.98/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| RTX 4090 | $0.20/hr | nafnaf | — unchanged |
| A100 80GB | $1.09/hr | Thunder Compute | — unchanged |

Read the terms before you chase the floor — minimum commitments and community-cloud availability differ from list-rate clouds. But the fact stands: on Oct 26 you could still rent an H100 for roughly half the rate a rising list price asks ($2.25 vs $4.50–$4.61). Rising list prices have not pulled the floor up — yet.

...

### How we know

GPUJournal reads providers' own published pricing pages and banks the figures at every check. The checks behind this page fell on Oct 19, 22, 23, 24 and 26, 2026 — there are gaps between them, so the October rises are documented check by check rather than day by day. A price change we catch in our own checks is only reported when both the before and after figures were seen on the provider's own page, each with its date; that is how the Verda and RunPod rises above were verified. The Nebius rise of Oct 1, 2026 is different: it predates our records and was an announced rise, so we did not bank both sides of it ourselves — we verified the post-rise rates on Nebius's own page (checked Oct 19, re-read unchanged Oct 26) and report it as announced. And a price a provider merely states about itself never appears on our board as a verified price. Where a provider's pages state figures we cannot verify, Price Watch reports them labelled as stated — which is how disagreements get exposed rather than hidden: on Oct 26, Spheron's pages stated the same H100 at $2.64 on some pages and $2.98 on others, and we report the disagreement rather than pick a number.
